title: Carpet shampoo and hot-water extraction: step sequence and drying
audience: Cleaners who shampoo and extract carpet with a hand-wand unit or a walk-behind extractor, once the method has been chosen under the carpet course.
learningOutcomes: Sequence a carpet shampoo and extraction job from debris removal through to drying and handover.
Control solution volume, the area treated per pass and the recovery-tank level so the carpet dries without damage to furniture or the carpet.
Recognise machine and electrical faults that require the machine to be stopped and reported.

instruction.heading: Preparation before any solution goes down
instruction.body: Vacuum first, so loose grit is lifted before shampoo goes down and cannot turn into muddy residue. Shift the furniture to a suitable spot, and inspect the carpet for marks needing pre-treatment. Lift chewing gum with a scraper before wet work begins. Put up signage and a barrier before the unit is wheeled in.

instruction.heading: Making up the solution and adding defoamer
instruction.body: Mix the shampoo in the tank following the product label, and put the defoamer into the recovery tank before extraction begins, so foam does not reach the motor. Never let the unit run without solution, and never drive it over its own cord. Use no more water than the method specifies; surplus water prolongs drying and complicates finishing.

instruction.heading: Working in small sections
instruction.body: On a walk-behind extractor, work roughly three square metres per section. Keep any pre-sprayed patch to around twenty square metres or less, so the solution is still moist when you extract it. Begin at the spot most distant from the exit and move back toward it, so you do not tread on finished carpet.

instruction.heading: Extraction passes
instruction.body: With a hand-wand machine, pull the wand back slowly with the suction engaged, and repeat the pass over the same ground to take out the solution. On a heavy stain, make a second extraction pass over the same spot to lift more soil. Empty the recovery tank before it reaches its fill line. A full recovery tank loses suction and leaves the carpet wet.

instruction.heading: Drying and close-down
instruction.body: Let the carpet dry fully before furniture is returned. When the job ends, drain and flush the water tank, clean the water jet after every use, and wipe the unit down. For a battery unit, plug it into the charger as the maker specifies. Store the unit in its assigned place.

procedure: Run the vacuum over the carpet to clear loose debris.
Move the furniture to a suitable spot, pre-treat any marks, and lift chewing gum with a scraper.
Dress in the protective gear the label and site rules specify, and erect the signage and barrier.
Mix the shampoo to the product label, and put defoamer into the recovery tank.
Check the unit and its cord, and connect it through an earth leakage device before plugging it in.
Apply solution to a section of about three square metres, and keep any pre-sprayed area to about twenty square metres or less.
Make extraction passes in slow, steady strokes, and repeat over stains. Empty the recovery tank before it fills.
Turn the unit off and unplug it. Drain and flush the water tank, then rinse the wand and jet.
Leave the carpet to dry, and do not return furniture until it is dry. Record the drying status at handover.
Take off the PPE, put the equipment away, and wash your hands.

workedExamples.situation: A walk-behind extractor's recovery tank is nearly full halfway down a room, and the carpet in the first area is still wet.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop. Turn the unit off, empty the recovery tank, and check the cord and hoses before going on. Work in smaller sections from here. Do not add more solution to carpet that is already wet, and confirm the drying status before any furniture goes back.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks for the furniture to go back the same afternoon, while the carpet is still damp.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you tell the customer?
workedExamples.reasoning: Explain that the carpet must dry before the furniture goes back, and agree a drying time with the customer. Record the drying status and any ventilation advice you gave. Do not return furniture onto wet carpet.

equipmentAndPpe: Extraction unit fitted with the right tools for the method (hand-wand or walk-behind)
Carpet shampoo and defoamer, used as the product label directs
Spot cleaner and a scraper for chewing gum
Earth leakage device (safety switch) connected before the unit is plugged in
Gloves and eye protection, and a mask where the product label requires one

commonErrors.error: Running the unit on dry carpet, or letting it run dry.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep solution flowing onto the carpet while the unit works, and stop if the solution runs out.

commonErrors.error: Pre-spraying too large an area before extracting it.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the pre-sprayed area to a size you can extract before it dries.

commonErrors.error: Returning furniture before the carpet has dried.
commonErrors.prevention: Wait for the carpet to dry, and record the drying status at handover.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The unit must be connected through an earth leakage device, the cord kept clear of its path, and the electrical checks in “Safe use and care of electrical machines” followed. Hands must be dry when the plug is connected or disconnected.
Solution dilution, dwell time and PPE are set by the product label and safety data sheet.
The timings given in the reference document are rough estimates, not Australian benchmarks. This lesson uses none of them.

qualityStandard: Visible debris is removed before any solution is applied.
Solution and defoamer are used as the product label directs.
The carpet is dry before furniture is returned.
The unit and its cord are inspected before use, and any fault is reported.
documentationEvidence: Area record with the method and product used
Drying status and time recorded at handover
Fault or defect report for any machine or carpet issue
summary: Vacuum, pre-treat, shampoo in sections, extract, empty, then dry.
Watch the solution volume, the area per pass and the recovery-tank level.
Stop on machine or electrical faults and report them.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the purpose of vacuuming before any solution is applied?
options: It is optional if the carpet looks clean and the shampoo will still lift it.
It lifts loose grit so the shampoo does not turn it into a muddy residue.
It replaces the defoamer, which is only needed later in the process.

knowledgeChecks.question: The recovery tank of a walk-behind unit fills during a pass. What is the correct response?
options: Keep going, and empty it at the end of the room so the pass is not interrupted
Stop, empty the recovery tank, and check the cord and hoses before continuing.
Add more solution to speed up the pass and keep the carpet moving steadily

knowledgeChecks.question: When may furniture be moved back onto the carpet?
options: As soon as the last extraction pass finishes.
Once the carpet has dried, and the drying status has been recorded.
As soon as the customer asks, even if the carpet is still wet.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say about running the carpet unit?
options: Run it dry to clear the hoses
Run it with the tank open
Drive it over its own cord to save time
Never let the unit run without solution
